classification.primary: Terminal preflight refusal because a Rust command was active. This is an environment scheduling refusal before candidate materialization, not a compile failure, test failure, timeout, or unknown completion.
classification.secondary: The unconditional read-only-reference cleanup reports a baseline-missing comparison as donor metadata change. It does not establish an actual donor change.
classification.candidate_qualification: No compilation or behavioral evidence was produced for this candidate by this attempt; no previous result may be transferred to it.

source_control_flow.fact: RUST_PREFLIGHT scans /proc comm/cwd, prints its own UID and active process entries, and exits 1 when the active list is nonempty. It does not signal or alter those processes.

raw(..., check=True) waits for and records the original launcher result and raises immediately on nonzero exit. A reported exit 1 is a terminal refusal, distinct from its explicit timeout/unknown branch.
The idle preflight call is before reference_before assignment, clone/fetch/checkout and source_ready. On that refusal, reference_before remains absent and candidate setup is unreachable.

The exception is recorded as failed. source_ready/root_setup_started/root_touched_records remain false, so source inventory, Root mount setup cleanup and Root record ownership cleanup are not entered. WORK/RECORDS and raw preflight evidence may already exist.

identity(REFERENCE) returns a dictionary of HEAD/tree/status. reference_unchanged assigns reference_after then compares result.get('reference_before') against it. With no before key, None differs from any successful identity dictionary, generating the secondary message even if the repository never changed.

limits: The after identity is a point-in-time clean observation, not a valid within-attempt before/after proof.
This review does not assert that the donor changed, nor certify unchanged donor bytes without a recorded baseline.
Keep the original exit, raw log, progress and secondary cleanup error intact, with this explanation alongside them.
